timeline: Argentina open with a shock loss to Saudi Arabia, then win every match through the knockouts.
Messi captains the side through Australia, the Netherlands and Croatia, playing some of the best football of his career at 35.
The final against France swings wildly: Argentina lead 2-0, Mbappé scores twice in two minutes to force extra time, then completes a hat-trick.
Argentina win 4-2 on penalties. Messi lifts the trophy that had eluded him, finally completing his career.
A 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé announces himself, scoring in the round of 16 rout of Argentina and again in the final.
Croatia, led by Luka Modrić, reach their first ever final after three straight extra-time knockout wins.
France control the final 4-2, helped by a deflected free kick and a rare World Cup final own goal.
Didier Deschamps becomes only the third man to win the World Cup as both player and coach.

tagline: The Mineirazo and a Götze winner
timeline: Hosts Brazil are stunned 7-1 by Germany in the semi-final, one of the most lopsided results in World Cup history.
Germany carry that momentum into the final against Messi's Argentina.
Mario Götze volleys in a Schürrle cross seven minutes from the end of extra time.
Germany become the first European team to win a World Cup held in the Americas.
Spain lose their opening match to Switzerland, then win every remaining game 1-0.
Their tiki-taka possession style, built around Xavi and Iniesta, defines the tournament.
A tense, foul-heavy final against the Netherlands stays goalless deep into extra time.
Andrés Iniesta scores in the 116th minute, giving Spain their first World Cup.
Zinedine Zidane, in his last professional match, scores a cheeky panenka penalty to open the scoring.
Marco Materazzi equalises for Italy soon after with a header.
In extra time Zidane headbutts Materazzi in the chest and is sent off, ending his career in red.
Italy win the shootout 5-3 to claim their fourth title.
The first World Cup held in Asia, and the first co-hosted by two nations.
Ronaldo, recovering from career-threatening knee injuries, top-scores with eight goals.
He scores both goals in the final against Germany, completing a personal comeback four years after a mysterious final-day collapse in 1998.
Brazil claim a record fifth title.
Hosts France build a side around Zidane, Deschamps and Petit.
Brazil's Ronaldo suffers a still-unexplained fit hours before the final and is a shadow of himself on the pitch.
Zidane heads in two first-half goals, and Petit adds a third late on.
France win their first World Cup on home soil.
The World Cup's first visit to the United States draws record aggregate attendance.
Brazil, built around Romário and Bebeto, go unbeaten through the tournament.
The final against Italy is goalless after 120 minutes, the first World Cup final to reach a shootout.
Roberto Baggio skies the decisive penalty over the bar, and Brazil win their fourth title.
A tournament remembered for defensive, foul-heavy football and two red cards in the final.
Defending champions Argentina, without the injured backbone of 1986, scrape through on penalties twice.
Andreas Brehme converts a contentious late penalty for West Germany.
West Germany win their third title, days before German reunification.
Diego Maradona produces one of the greatest individual tournaments in history.
In the quarter-final against England he scores the 'Hand of God' goal with his fist, then minutes later the 'Goal of the Century', dribbling past five defenders.
He sets up the winner in the semi-final and scores twice in the final.
Argentina hold off a West German comeback to win 3-2.
Paolo Rossi returns from a match-fixing suspension and is quiet early on.
He then scores a hat-trick to eliminate favourites Brazil in one of the sport's great matches.
Rossi adds two more against Poland in the semi-final and opens the scoring in the final.
Italy beat West Germany 3-1 to win their third title, with Rossi taking the Golden Boot and Golden Ball.

tagline: Home glory under a military junta
timeline: Argentina host the tournament under a military dictatorship, and win amid later-confirmed allegations of match manipulation in the second round.
The Netherlands, without star Johan Cruyff who declined to play, reach a second straight final.
Mario Kempes scores twice in extra time for the hosts.
Argentina win their first World Cup.
The Netherlands, playing Rinus Michels' influential 'Total Football', take the lead inside two minutes without West Germany touching the ball.
West Germany, led by Franz Beckenbauer and Gerd Müller, respond and turn the game around before half time.
Müller scores the winner just before the break.
West Germany hold on to win their second title on home soil.
Pelé, at his third and final World Cup, leads a Brazil side widely regarded as the greatest ever assembled.
Brazil win every match of the tournament.
The final against Italy features a flowing team goal finished by captain Carlos Alberto.
Brazil win a third title and keep the Jules Rimet Trophy permanently, as per the rules of the time.
Hosts England reach their first World Cup final, having conceded only three goals all tournament.
West Germany equalise in the final's last minute of normal time to force extra time.
Geoff Hurst scores twice more in extra time, including a shot off the crossbar whose goal-line status is still debated.
Hurst remains the only player to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final. England win their only title.
Pelé is injured early in the tournament and misses most of it.
Garrincha steps up as the tournament's outstanding player, driving Brazil through the knockout rounds.
Brazil overturn an early deficit in the final against Czechoslovakia.
Brazil retain the title, becoming the first team to win back-to-back World Cups since 1938.
A 17-year-old Pelé becomes the youngest player to appear in a World Cup, then the youngest to score and to win it.
Brazil introduce a back-four formation that influences tactics for years afterward.
Pelé scores twice in the final, including a celebrated chest-and-volley goal.
Brazil win their first World Cup, played outside South America.
Hungary's 'Mighty Magyars', unbeaten in four years, thrash West Germany 8-3 in the group stage.
The two sides meet again in the final.
West Germany fall behind early but fight back to win 3-2, denying a Hungary team many consider the best never to win the trophy.
The result is remembered in Germany as the 'Miracle of Bern'.
The tournament uses a final round-robin group rather than a single final; Brazil only need a draw against Uruguay to win at home.
Nearly 200,000 fans pack the Maracanã expecting a home celebration.
Uruguay come back from 1-0 down to win 2-1, silencing the stadium.
The result, still called the Maracanazo, remains one of the sport's great upsets.
Italy travel and win it again, becoming the first team to retain the World Cup.
Playing under Fascist Italy, the squad faces political pressure to win.
Gino Colaussi and Silvio Piola each score twice in the final.
Italy beat Hungary 4-2, and the trophy is not contested again until 1950 due to the Second World War.
The first World Cup to use a straight knockout format after qualifying.
Hosts Italy, managed by Vittorio Pozzo, are pushed by Czechoslovakia in the final.
Czechoslovakia lead with 20 minutes left before Italy equalise and win in extra time.
Italy claim their first title on home soil.
The inaugural World Cup is held in Uruguay, chosen partly to mark 100 years of Uruguayan independence.
Thirteen teams enter, mostly from the Americas, as the long boat journey deters several European sides.
Hosts Uruguay meet neighbours Argentina in the final in front of a crowd in Montevideo.
Uruguay win 4-2 to become the first World Cup champions.
